newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB awaits 10-yr bond sale for next move.
newsitem.headline: JGB awaits 10-yr bond sale for next move.

text.p: The cash and futures Japanese government bond (JGB) market is waiting for the outcome of a scheduled 10-year bond auction due at 2330 GMT to decide the next direction, traders said.
"The Feds' steady policy decision, though widely expected in the JGB market, will lend psychological support to the market," said a trader at a city bank's brokerage affiliate.

The Ministry of Finance is expected to offer 1.6 trillion yen worth of 10-year JGBs, of which about 60 percent is to be issued through the auction. Bond traders said the prospective coupon is 2.9 percent.
The prospective coupon rate compares with a 3.1 percent coupon for the September bond.
Traders said the auction is likely to attract modest demand from banks, though the likely coupon rate is too low to be held by portfolio accounts at institutional investors.
Hedge selling in the December contract against the new 10-year bond was detected on Tuesday. Those positions are likely be covered if the auction is successful, traders said.
The next target for December is 122.65, the record high for the benchmark futures contract, hit on July 7, 1995.
